scope: Body-only independent reading of the ten additional sets. Gold, teaching, hints and author reviewer outputs omitted. No human approval.

sentences: Many schools now ban phones during lunch breaks, hoping students will talk to each other more.
Some parents worry that such rules treat teenagers like small children.
Yet the evidence from schools that tried the ban is hard to ignore.
Students in these schools report fewer conflicts and more conversations at their tables.
Rules that feel strict at first can protect the very freedom to connect face to face.
Schools should therefore keep phones out of lunch breaks, even when some students complain.

sentences: When a city plants trees along a busy street, the most obvious benefit is shade.
But the trees also slow down drivers, who sense the road as narrower.
Shop owners on tree-lined streets often see more people walking past their windows.
Even the noise from traffic seems softer behind a row of leaves.
In short, a street tree does far more work than simply blocking the sun.

sentences: The Lindale Science Fair is open to students aged 12 to 18.
Each team may have up to three members and must submit one project.
Projects must be registered online by May 10, and late entries will not be accepted.
Judges will score projects on originality, method, and clarity of presentation.
The top three teams will receive science kits and a visit to a local laboratory.

sentences: Mira had practiced the piano piece for weeks, but on stage her hands began to shake.
She missed a note in the second line and felt the room go silent.
Then she remembered her teacher's words: the music does not stop for a mistake.
She kept playing, and by the last page her fingers moved as if on their own.
When the applause came, she realized she had been carrying the wrong fear all along.

sentences: Researchers asked two groups to memorize a list of words.
One group simply reread the list several times, while the other covered it and tried to recall the words.
A week later, the recall group remembered far more words than the rereading group.
Interestingly, the rereading group had felt more confident right after studying.
The effort of pulling information out of memory, not the comfort of seeing it again, made learning last.
[요약] Trying to (A) information, rather than reviewing it, leads to more (B) learning.

sentences: A small bakery once decided to stop offering twenty kinds of bread.
Instead, it focused on just five loaves made with great care.
Customers who used to stand undecided now chose quickly and returned more often.
The owner noticed that fewer choices also meant less waste at the end of each day.
Sometimes, ________ is what makes a business stronger rather than weaker.

sentences: Many people believe that a quiet room is always the best place to concentrate.
It is true that sudden, sharp noises such as a slammed door can break our attention.
Yet a steady background hum often helps us focus rather than hurting our work.
In one experiment, writers produced more original ideas in a café-like murmur than in near silence.
A low, constant sound seems to loosen our thinking just enough to let unusual connections form.
The ideal workspace, then, may be not a silent one but one with a gentle, even noise.
body.stem: 글을 읽고 문장마다 하는 일과 글 전체 구조를 고르시오.

sentences: Member-owned grocery stores offer rural towns a practical way to keep fresh food within reach.
Over the past decade, many small towns in the region have lost their only supermarket.
Chains close such stores because the profits are too thin to satisfy distant shareholders.
A member-owned store faces no such pressure, since its owners are also its customers.
They are content as long as the shelves stay full and the doors stay open.
In one village of eight hundred people, residents bought shares for fifty dollars each.
Within a year, the shop that a chain had abandoned was selling bread and vegetables again.
body.stem: 글을 읽고 문장마다 하는 일과 글 전체 구조를 고르시오.

sentences: Researchers asked two groups of students to learn the same list of foreign words.
One group studied for an hour in a single session, while the other spread the same hour over four days.
A week later, the second group recalled nearly twice as many words.
Spacing apparently gives memories time to settle between sessions.
Students who want their learning to last should therefore break their review into short sessions spread across several days.
body.stem: 글을 읽고 문장마다 하는 일과 글 전체 구조를 고르시오.

sentences: Old maps record what people once feared as well as where they traveled.
Mapmakers rarely left the unknown parts of a chart blank.
Instead, they filled those spaces with whatever their culture imagined might be there.
A sixteenth-century chart of the Atlantic shows sea serpents in the very waters sailors dreaded most.
Another map from the same period places a land of giants beyond the southern edge of the known world.
Neither image was meant as decoration.
Each marked a danger that readers of the time took seriously.
In this sense, the empty spaces of an old map say as much about its makers as its coastlines do.
body.stem: 글을 읽고 문장마다 하는 일과 글 전체 구조를 고르시오.

sentences: Electric scooters have clearly made short trips across the city faster and cheaper.
It is true that riders no longer need to wait for a bus to travel a few blocks.
Even so, the scooters are creating more problems on sidewalks than they solve on the roads.
Parked scooters often lie across walkways, blocking people who use wheelchairs.
Pedestrians also report being startled by riders who pass them at high speed.
Last spring, an elderly man in one downtown district broke his wrist after tripping over a scooter left at a bus stop.
body.stem: 글을 읽고 문장마다 하는 일과 글 전체 구조를 고르시오.

sentences: In many offices, praise is handed out only after a large project is finished.
This habit quietly drains motivation during the long months in between.
Without any sign that their daily work is noticed, employees begin to wonder whether it matters.
Many respond by doing only what is strictly required.
By the time the project ends and the praise finally arrives, the best effort has already been lost.
Delayed recognition, in other words, costs a team the very energy it is meant to reward.
body.stem: 글을 읽고 문장마다 하는 일과 글 전체 구조를 고르시오.

sentences: Many people believe that a messy desk is a sure sign of a disorganized mind.
The image of the tidy, efficient worker is so familiar that few stop to question it.
Yet observations of office workers suggest that the link is far weaker than we assume.
Some people who work among piles of paper can find any document within seconds, because the piles follow an order that only they need to understand.
Their desks look chaotic to visitors, but the arrangement reflects how recently and how often each item is used.
Judging a person's thinking by the surface of a desk, then, tells us more about our expectations than about the worker.
body.stem: 글을 읽고 문장마다 하는 일과 글 전체 구조를 고르시오.

sentences: Small-town libraries face a serious problem: fewer and fewer people walk through their doors.
Most residents now find information online and see little reason to make the trip.
As visits fall, councils cut library budgets, which leads to shorter opening hours and even fewer visitors.
One way to break this cycle is to offer what a screen cannot, such as spaces where people make and repair things together.
In one town, part of the library became a workshop where residents could borrow tools and join weekly repair classes.
Volunteers taught everything from fixing bicycles to sewing torn clothes.
Within two years, the building was busier than it had been in decades.
body.stem: 글을 읽고 문장마다 하는 일과 글 전체 구조를 고르시오.

sentences: A new highway can reshape a quiet village faster than any decision made by the village itself.
Once city drivers can reach it in an hour, the village becomes a popular weekend stop.
Cafés and small shops open along the main road, and land prices begin to climb.
Young families who had planned to stay may find that they can no longer afford a home.
Older residents, meanwhile, often find new part-time work in the growing businesses.
body.stem: 글을 읽고 문장마다 하는 일과 글 전체 구조를 고르시오.

sentences: Travelers today can choose between a printed map and a navigation app.
A printed map shows a whole region at once.
The reader therefore builds a picture of how places relate to one another.
That picture takes effort to form, but it often lasts long after the trip.
A navigation app gives one instruction at a time and asks the traveler to look only at the next turn.
It saves effort and rarely lets anyone get lost.
Yet it leaves little behind in memory once the screen goes dark.
The real choice, then, is between arriving quickly and coming to know the place.
body.stem: 글을 읽고 문장마다 하는 일과 글 전체 구조를 고르시오.

sentences: Ms. Lee, a primary school teacher, had long wondered whether her brightly decorated classroom actually helped her pupils learn.
To find out, she and a university researcher taught the same science lessons to two groups of nine-year-olds, one in a room covered with posters and one in a room with almost bare walls.
The children in the decorated room spent more time looking away from the lesson and scored lower on the final tests.
Those in the plain room stayed on task longer and remembered more of what they had been taught.
The finding suggests that what surrounds young learners can quietly compete with the lesson for their attention.
Teachers who want young students to focus might therefore think twice before filling every wall with decorations.
body.stem: 글을 읽고 문장마다 하는 일과 글 전체 구조를 고르시오.

sentences: Animals often survive harsh winters by changing their behavior rather than their bodies.
Some squirrels bury thousands of seeds in autumn and return to them, one by one, when snow covers the ground.
Certain birds gather in tight groups at night, sharing the warmth of their bodies until morning.
Honeybees cluster around their queen and shiver their muscles to keep the center of the hive warm.
None of these creatures grows a thicker coat; each simply acts in a way that makes the cold easier to bear.
body.stem: 글을 읽고 문장마다 하는 일과 글 전체 구조를 고르시오.

sentences: City planners once chose street trees mainly for how quickly they grew.
Fast-growing species filled empty sidewalks within a few years, which pleased residents who wanted shade.
However, many of these trees had weak wood and shallow roots, so storms often brought them down onto cars and power lines.
Some cities have therefore begun planting a mix of slower species that live longer and resist wind.
Critics complain that this practice leaves streets looking bare for nearly a decade.
Supporters reply that a tree which survives eighty years provides far more shade over its life than two or three quick replacements ever could.
In their view, patience at the start is the price of a canopy that lasts for generations.
body.stem: 밑줄 친 'this practice'가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

planting a mix of slow, long-lived species
clearing fallen trees from cars and power lines
filling empty sidewalks with shade very quickly
strengthening shallow roots against heavy storms

sentences: Students preparing for an exam usually choose between two broad strategies.
Some reread their notes several times until the material begins to feel familiar.
Others close the book and try to write down everything they remember, checking afterward what they missed.
Most learners prefer the first strategy because it feels smooth and produces a comforting sense of progress.
Yet experiments repeatedly show that the latter leads to better results on tests given a week later.
The effort of pulling information out of memory seems to strengthen it, whereas easy rereading leaves little trace.
What feels productive, in other words, is not always what actually works.
body.stem: 밑줄 친 'the latter'가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: rereading notes until they feel familiar
a comforting sense of steady progress
tests that are given a week later
recalling material unaided, then checking gaps
choosing between two broad strategies

sentences: Doctors have long noticed that some patients feel better after taking pills that contain no medicine at all.
This effect is usually explained by expectation: believing that a treatment will work changes how the body responds.
Researchers were therefore surprised when patients improved even after being told openly that their pills were inactive.
In such cases, expectation cannot easily be the whole story, since the patients knew there was nothing to expect.
One proposal is that the ritual of treatment itself, such as visiting a clinic and swallowing a pill, triggers learned responses.
If so, the setting in which medicine is given may matter more than doctors have generally assumed.
body.stem: 밑줄 친 'such cases'가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: patients improving though told their pills were inactive
patients improving because they expect treatment to work
doctors delivering care in an ordinary clinic setting
pills that contain real and effective medicine
the body's general response to belief in treatment

sentences: Bees that discover a rich patch of flowers return to the hive and perform a special dance.
The angle of the dance tells other workers in which direction to fly, and its length signals the distance.
For a long time, scientists assumed that every bee watching the dance simply followed its instructions.
Recent observations, however, suggest a more complicated picture.
Experienced foragers often ignore the dance and return to familiar sites, even when those sites have dried up.
Only when their old flowers have failed several times do they pay attention to the dancers.
Younger bees, by contrast, rely on the dance almost from their first flight.
body.stem: 밑줄 친 'they'가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the dancers back from rich flower patches
younger bees on their very first flights
the scientists who observed the hive
the old flowers that have dried up
experienced foragers loyal to familiar sites

sentences: When a new road is built to relieve traffic, drivers who once avoided the area start using it.
Some people who used to take the train switch to driving, and others make trips they would not have made before.
Within a few years, the new road is often as crowded as the old one was.
Transportation researchers have observed this so consistently that they treat it as a rule rather than an exception.
The lesson for city governments is uncomfortable but clear.
Adding lanes rarely solves congestion for long, because the extra space itself creates new demand for travel.
body.stem: 밑줄 친 'this'가 가리키는 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: commuters giving up the train service
city governments deciding to add lanes

drivers avoiding a congested area
a rule applied in transport research

sentences: Museums face a constant choice about how to display fragile objects.
One option is to keep them behind glass in dim light, which protects them but makes them hard to see.
Another is to show high-quality copies in the open while the originals stay safely in storage.
Visitors can then examine every detail, and the originals suffer no damage at all.
Many curators, however, hesitate to adopt the method.
They worry that people come to museums precisely to stand in front of the real thing, and that a copy, however perfect, cannot provide that experience.
For these curators, authenticity is worth some loss of visibility.
body.stem: 밑줄 친 'the method'가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: keeping objects behind glass in dim light
showing copies while originals stay stored
examining every detail of the originals
standing in front of the real objects
choosing how to display fragile items

sentences: Every year our school sends a small team to a national contest.
